author: serenita_io
content:
Thanks for everyone's input on ACDT today.

One new issue was brought up by <@586161934425128960> : the VC cannot verify that the bid it received can be covered by the builder.

This happens in the case the node operator's VC connects to a builder that ends up sending it bids that it can't cover.

What would currently happen in a case like this is the VC would supply the bid to the beacon node, the beacon node would refute it as invalid and fall back to a different bid (p2p bid or local payload). This does grieve other (especially direct) builders that may have submitted a valid bid to the VC.

We want to encourage people to connect to as many direct builders as possible, and the above attack means people will want to do the opposite.

I believe an actual attack like this would likely be discovered pretty quickly and everyone would quickly stop connecting to the builder that created it. However, if we don't want to rely on this "social" mechanism, there are a few things we could do to protect against it:

A) The VC would supply not one, but all the bids it received to its connected beacon nodes. The beacon node would then select the first valid bid out of the list to include in the block. The only downside is it could make the request big, but bids are tiny objects so this is not a huge concern.

B) The VC would keep track of builder balances. Even if only done once an epoch or so, it would make it significantly more difficult to pull of the griefing attack described above.

A) sounds slightly better to me at the moment. Let me know your thoughts.
